title: Data lake, lakehouse and Delta Lake

videos.script: A warehouse decides the shape of the data before it lets any in. A data lake does the opposite: it keeps every file as it arrived, and decides later. {{lake}} That is its strength. A new source is a folder, not a project. Logs, images, files from partners, all of it, cheaply, in object storage. {{strength}} And it is its weakness. Files are not a table. Nothing stops two programs writing at once. Nothing says which files are current. Nothing refuses a file with the wrong columns. A lake without discipline becomes a swamp. {{swamp}} The fix is small and clever. Keep the files, and add a log beside them: a list of commits, each saying which files were added and which removed. {{log}} Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg and Apache Hudi are three versions of that idea. With one of them, a folder of Parquet files can be updated, read as it was yesterday, and protected from a bad append. {{formats}} Ana builds a Delta table out of the shop's sales, corrects one line in it, travels back in time, and watches it refuse a file with one column too many. {{build}} A lake with tables in it is called a lakehouse. The warehouse's model still sits on top. {{lakehouse}}
